terms.definition: Dishonestly making a false representation, intending to make a gain or cause a loss.
terms.examiner: The offence is complete when the representation is made: no one has to be deceived and nothing has to be gained.

terms.definition: Any statement of fact or law, including a statement about a state of mind, made expressly or by conduct, including to a machine.
terms.examiner: DPP v Ray and R v Lambie show representation by conduct; s2(5) covers representations to machines.

terms.definition: Untrue or misleading, where the person making it knows that it is, or might be, untrue or misleading.
terms.examiner: The knowledge requirement is part of the actus reus test and is often missed.

terms.term: Fraud by failing to disclose information (s3)
terms.definition: Dishonestly failing to disclose information that one is under a legal duty to disclose, intending to make a gain or cause a loss.
terms.examiner: The duty can come from statute, the type of transaction, a contract or custom.

terms.definition: Dishonestly abusing a position in which one is expected to safeguard the financial interests of another, intending a gain or loss.
terms.examiner: The position can be formal (trustee, employee) or informal; R v Marshall concerned a care worker.

terms.definition: Obtaining services by a dishonest act, knowing they are to be paid for and intending not to pay in full.
terms.examiner: Unlike ss2–4, this needs a result: the service must actually be obtained.
